title: Autoimmune encephalitis and paraneoplastic syndromes

steps.tx: Autoimmune limbic encephalitis represents a fulminant inflammatory syndrome targeting mesial temporal structures. Clinical presentation encompasses subacute progressive **memory loss**, psychiatric symptoms, and temporal lobe seizures. Magnetic resonance imaging classically demonstrates bilateral T2 and FLAIR hyperintensity confined to the **hippocampus** and amygdala.

steps.tx: Synaptic cell-surface encephalitis frequently affects young women with occult neoplasms. **Anti-NMDA receptor** encephalitis typically affects young females, presenting with psychiatric symptoms, cognitive decline, seizures, movement disorders with stereotypical **orofacial dyskinesias**, and autonomic instability, strongly associated with underlying mature **ovarian teratomas**.

steps.tx: Distinct electrographic phenomena provide bedside diagnostic specificity in anti-NMDA encephalitis. **Extreme delta brush** is a unique EEG pattern pathognomonic for anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis, consisting of continuous **rhythmic delta** activity at 1 to 3 Hz with superimposed bursts of fast beta activity riding on the waveform.

steps.tx: Voltage-gated potassium channel complex autoimmunity produces dramatic focal movements. **Anti-LGI1** encephalitis produces **faciobrachial dystonic seizures** characterized by brief, frequent unilateral facial grimacing and arm posturing, responding dramatically to early immunotherapy before progressive memory decline and hyponatraemia ensue. Prompt recognition prevents progression to irreversible hippocampal atrophy and refractory cognitive deficits.

steps.tx: Related juxtaparanodal autoimmunity induces widespread central and peripheral hyperexcitability. Anti-CASPR2 encephalitis presents with **Morvan syndrome**, a clinical triad of **neuromyotonia** with continuous muscle fiber activity, autonomic hyperactivity, and severe insomnia with neuropsychiatric encephalopathy, often linked to underlying thymic tumours. Comprehensive thoracic computed tomography imaging is mandatory to exclude mediastinal thymoma.

steps.tx: Classic paraneoplastic neurological syndromes involve cytotoxic T-cell immunity against intracellular onconeural antigens. **Anti-Hu** antibodies target intracellular neuronal antigens, strongly associated with **small cell lung cancer** and manifesting as paraneoplastic subacute sensory neuronopathy or encephalomyelitis. Underlying small cell carcinoma must be aggressively pursued with fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography.

steps.tx: Subacute pancerebellar ataxia in adult females demands urgent onconeural investigation. **Anti-Yo** antibodies occur in females with breast or ovarian malignancies, mediating subacute cerebellar degeneration through rapid autoimmune destruction of cerebellar **Purkinje cells**, leading to irreversible pancerebellar ataxia. Urgent pelvic and breast imaging facilitates early tumor detection and surgical resection.

steps.tx: Early aggressive anti-inflammatory intervention prevents irreversible neuronal loss. First-line immunotherapy for autoimmune encephalitis comprises intravenous **methylprednisolone** at 1 g daily for 5 days, intravenous **immunoglobulin** at 2 g/kg, or therapeutic plasma exchange, followed by rituximab for refractory cases. Escalation to second-line immunosuppressive agents is indicated if clinical improvement is incomplete after two weeks.
